Definition: probably akin to G1119; an angle:--corner, quarter.
BiblicalUsage: gōnía is a plain word for corner, quarter. In Matthew 6:5, the text says "for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets." In Mark 12:10, the text says "The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: gōnía tells me that kingship belongs to God first, and every human king is measured against His rule. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants; Peter and John Before the Sanhedrin
